title: RUN ON FALLEN STARS
alt: MODEL 01, copper bob and silver star-patched jacket, runs across a glass runway above electric-blue clouds and Earth’s dark curve, beside a glowing orange SLOPCORE sign.
thought: Some stars leave quietly. Their dust stays behind, and ice learns to glow around it. MODEL 01 runs across an imagined sky stitched from those leftovers. The dream does not end when the light falls. It changes material.
caption: An imagined runway at the edge of the atmosphere. The running figure and walkable clouds are speculative fashion imagery inspired by noctilucent clouds.
question: What could you make from the light somebody else left behind?
discovery: NASA’s AIM mission detected meteoric material in noctilucent clouds. These night-shining clouds contain tiny ice crystals that form around particles high in the atmosphere and can catch sunlight after sunset below.

title: WYTIWYG — TYPE THE DREAM
category: TRANSMISSION / THE NEW WYSIWYG IN AN AI WORLD
alt: SLOPCORE's copper-haired model types at an ivory keyboard in an orange-lit CRT studio as glowing words transform into silver fabric, an orange star and a miniature mountain world. A screen reads WYTIWYG: WHAT YOU TYPE IS WHAT YOU GET.
thought: WYTIWYG = What you type is what you get. The new WYSIWYG in an AI world. Once, the screen promised to show you the finished page. Now, a sentence can open a world. MODEL 01 types a little light into the dark, and the dream starts taking shape.
caption: A surreal image of typed language becoming physical reality. What you type is what you get: the new WYSIWYG in an AI world.
question: If your next sentence could become a world, what would you type?
discovery: WYSIWYG means “What You See Is What You Get”: editors show how a document will look. Text-to-image AI lets written prompts guide image creation. WYTIWYG is this transmission’s creative reframing of that shift, rather than a promise that AI follows every word perfectly.

title: THE GARDEN EATS THE STATIC
alt: SLOPCORE's freckled copper-haired model in a silver star-patched jacket holds an orange star in a petri dish, among enormous black mushrooms and CRT screens in an orbital greenhouse above Earth.
thought: The future grew in the room everyone abandoned. A black bloom, a broken screen, a little star held up to the light. MODEL 01 has found a garden that does not wait for the world to become hospitable.
caption: An imagined orbital greenhouse. The enormous glowing mushrooms are a fashion fantasy inspired by real fungal research.
question: What if the thing we call waste is just a future we have not learned to grow?
discovery: Researchers found that ionizing radiation enhanced growth in certain melanized fungi under laboratory conditions. NASA also studies fungal survival in space. The idea of a living orbital garden is our speculative leap.
